Assarmatori is an Italian shipowners’ association based in Rome, Italy. Members include both national and international shipowners and ship operators which, regardless of their flag State, work within the Italian maritime cluster.
Assarmatori represents a large part of the merchant fleet registered in Italy and some of the major shipping operators which maintain regular shipping services in Italy contributing to the overall Italian maritime cluster.
As a national shipping association, Assarmatori is concerned with all technical, legal, environmental, safety and training, employment affairs and trade policy issues that impact on ship and port operations.
We give voice to shipowners and operators on key maritime issues to improve business conditions and support investments for more efficient maritime services and development of new technologies.
We represent shipping interests at the national and international levels, especially with the EU’s institutions, governmental and intergovernmental bodies, international shipping associations and other key players and stakeholders.
Assarmatori’s goals are to:
- to maintain a dialogue between Members and to provide support to them in dealing with the politics and the public administrations at all levels in Italy and abroad.
- to foster a level global playing field to promote a competitive and open business environment in Italy in order to enhance the Blue Economy.
- to ensure that every kind of maritime service is properly represented, giving protection to international operators owning transport lines, operating terminals or passengers’ stations in the Italian ports.
- to ensure that the views of its members are properly presented and listened to by the national, European and international governing bodies and institutions.
- to conduct, as an employers’ association, collective bargaining negotiations with seafarers Unions in Italy.
- to promote sustainable technical development through the application of innovative systems that reduce the environmental impact of emissions.

description: ReCatalyst d.o.o. is developing a groundbreaking nanotechnology platform for producing advanced (electro)catalysts for fuel cells and water electrolysis, maximising the efficiency of platinum group metal use for decarbonisation of the energy and transport sectors with green hydrogen. It is a spin-out company from the National Institute of Chemistry (Ljubljana, Slovenia) founded in early 2021. The company holds a strong patented IP over flexible, customisable next-generation platinum-based catalyst solutions already proven in 19 customer pilots across hydrogen technologies value chains. We’ve invented and patented a process that cuts platinum usage by 60% without sacrificing performance. This efficiency also shrinks the fuel cell stack, reducing other components by 30% and overall production costs by 45%. Since inception, the company has received multiple awards such as the Slovenian Start-up-of-the-year 2023 and 2nd place at the EIT awards in the Venture section. The foundations of the start-up have been developed within the projects ERC ‘Proof of Concept’ StableCat and EIT Raw Materials Accelerator. In addition to the EIC Transition project ENABLER, the company has also successfully raised an oversubscribed Seed round of 1.7M EUR co-led by international investors HTGF, OCCIDENT and xista science ventures. ReCatalyst is actively building a global customer base, with projects already in five major G7 economies and across five continents. Among others, we also collaborate with chemical giants who enable large-scale manufacturing; 3 of the Big 6 are in active pilots with us. In the field of space applications, we would like to develop and use our nano technology in the Regenerative Fuel Cell (RFC).
entityDescription:
ReCatalyst is a spin-out (Start-up) company from National Institute of Chemistry (Ljubljana, Slovenia). Our core technology enables us to produce a wide variety of supported metal nanoparticle composites. The initial focus of the company are next-generation platinum-alloy PEM fuel cell catalysts. Our core mission is to make PEM fuel cells massively scalable by bringing the required platinum in PEM fuel cells down to the levels found in today's internal combustion engine vehicles. Additionally, another key competence of ReCatalyst also has a clear focus towards highly active, durable, and reliable catalyst materials and thus, the ability to provide customized solutions for also space applications.

Since incorporation in 2021, the team has reached a developed Minimum Viable Product as well as validated the scalability of their production process. description:
As a spin-off of the Tallinn University of Technology's Space Centre, Falconers' motto of "beating Moore's curse for sensing" was informed by the realization that much of (possible) satellite data is still under-communicated, under-processed and thus insufficiently valorized for end-users. Consequently, Falconers conducts its R&D at the intersection of sensing hardware and data processing, as both are needed for taking performance and efficacy to a new level. In ESA projects, we are interested in contributing with the following activities:

- Onboard processing

- AI image analysis

- Novel optronic sensors research

Falconers has experience from previous development projects in building remote sensing tools, multi-sensor integration and computing optimisation. We have participated in and led international R&D projects in various European formats, such as EDA novel optics OB-Study INOPTECH, where Falconers is prime contractor, and EDF STORE, EDF SPIDER and NATO SET-groups. 

Falconers' primary markets are defence ISR, forestry and agriculture. In the defence and ISR market, we develop HawkEye, an optical and computing payload for anomaly detection with a focus on camouflaged objects and decoys. HawkEye entered testing with the Estonian Defence Forces in Spring 2025. In forestry and agriculture, we develop FORSAIT, a remote sensing sensor fusion platform, integrating satellite and in-situ data, including multispectral drone imagery. FORSAIT has a fire simulation and anomaly detection capability, both from satellite and drone data.

entityDescription:
AIDIMME, Technological Institute on Metalworking, Wood, Furniture, Packaging and Related Industries is a non-profit R&D industrial association located in Valencia (Spain) with more than 40 years of experience contributing to the competitiveness of our companies.
With more than 160 employees (60% of them higher University graduates) and 25000m2 of technological infrastructure, the Institute is the technological extension of their associated companies. 
We are currently the technical umbrella organization for +640 associated companies in the mentioned sectors, with a strong regional character.
Our activity focuses both on research areas (in which AIDIMME has more than 25 labs and technical departments) and the current European priorities linked to our target sectors. 
Strategic Research Areas for AIDIMME include Circular Economy, Additive manufacturing, Industry 4.0, Product development and optimization, Advanced applications of materials, Biomaterials, Modified surfaces, Toxicity of materials and Intelligent packaging systems, while our Targeted Priorities include Green, Smart and Digitized Factory and Value Chain; Digital and Emerging Technologies; Clean Economy and Zero Pollution; Circular Economy and Bio-Economy
Biodiversity and Ecosystems; Secondary Raw Materials and Advanced Materials; Green, Resilient and Smart Buildings & Cities, and Clean, Resilient and Smart Mobility.
AIDIMME brings their companies a constant technological support (Data from 2023): 
• Different services are provided (more than 6000 actions of technical advice and consultancy, that include +45000 mechanical, chemical and endurance tests for products and materials, and around 60 technical courses) to our more than 1300 customers.
• We also developed 64 Research projects -10 international- last year. Both on an individual and collective basis- they are intended to expand the knowledge aplicable to the companies’ products and processes and get short-to-medium-term transferrable results.
• Additional actions include continuous information and dissemination, bespoke technology watch and contribution to standards.
